PullRequest.Title: sessions: clarify local computer labels

## Summary

Replace ambiguous standalone **Local** labels with **This Computer** across Agents workspace selection, local Agent Host choices, accessibility help, and the AI Customizations client group.

This makes it clearer that these choices refer to resources or processes on the current computer rather than a generic local scope.

Related: microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9975

## Validation

- Passed `npm run build-fast -- --client-only`
- Passed `npm run eslint -- src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/common/session.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/sessionWorkspacePicker.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationListWidget.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostTerminalContribution.ts`
- Passed `scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newChatWidget.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionWorkspacePicker.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionsChatAccessibilityHelp.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/agentHost/agentHostSessionConfigPicker.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsListFilters.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsRename.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsViewMenu.test.ts`
- Manually verified before/after states for the Agents workspace group, AI Customizations client group, and Agent Host terminal profile.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the New Chat provider/workspace picker and switch between host and Dev Container modes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider lookup, recent-workspace filtering, action construction, and picker rendering are synchronous. The changed literals only replace action/tab labels. Dev Container availability returns false immediately on a cold key and refreshes asynchronously, so its filesystem/IPC work remains off the initial picker critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check for a Dev Container configuration and Docker availability through provider.isDevContainerWorkspaceAvailable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold: at most one check per unique provider/workspace cache key, with at most four concurrent checks. Warm: zero checks while the boolean cache entry remains valid.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cached, limited availability check ran for the same recent workspaces; only the displayed Local/Use Local text differed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The picker does not await the check; it renders without the mode action and refreshes after resolution.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of registered providers and deduplicated recent workspaces. The work remains one synchronous list build plus cached availability checks per unique workspace, independent of the extra label characters.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider/action construction is synchronous. Existing Dev Container checks are coalesced by provider-plus-workspace key and pass through a shared Limiter(4); the diff changes neither behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The availability map stores both in-flight promises and resolved booleans under provider ID plus normalized folder URI. Label values are not part of the key, so cold/warm behavior and invalidation are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed lines feed only label fields/constants, while the existing boundary call, key, limiter, and async placement are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact recent-workspace counts and provider latency vary, but the diff does not alter either multiplicity or timing.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: label length changes do not add work, defeat the availability cache, increase fan-out, or move boundary work onto the critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Recompute and render Sessions list Environment and Created In filters
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A derived observable reads in-memory providers and sessions, constructs/sorts filter options, and registers menu items. The changed environment label participates only in displayed strings.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Environments, sessions, and discovered applications; existing construction is approximately environments times sessions plus sorting. The diff changes constant string contents only.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Entirely synchronous and serialized on the observable recomputation; no queue or concurrent boundary work is involved.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Structural equality suppresses unchanged derived menu state. Persisted filter keys use IDs, not labels, so the rename does not change storage keys, cache behavior, or recomputation frequency.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: getSessionFilterOptions is fully traced and performs only in-memory map, scan, sort, and localization operations on this path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large session catalogs can make the pre-existing recomputation more noticeable, but this PR does not increase catalog cardinality or algorithmic work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the same options are produced at the same frequency and complexity, with longer labels affecting only rendered text.

Scenarios.Scenario: Search and render AI Customizations grouped by client location
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the existing search debounce, loaded items are filtered, grouped, sorted, and committed to the tree. The changed literal supplies the remote-client group header label and does not alter matching, grouping keys, item count, or DOM-node count.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enqueue search telemetry for a non-empty customization search.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One telemetry event per completed debounced non-empty search, unchanged by group labels.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same search event was emitted after the same filter/group pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Telemetry is enqueued after filtering and is not introduced or multiplied by the changed label.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of loaded customization items and groups. Sorting/grouping complexity and rendered entry count are identical before and after the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Filtering/grouping is synchronous after the existing debounce; there is no newly scheduled work or changed parallelism.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The scenario operates on already loaded allItems and existing collapsed-group state; the changed label is not a cache key and creates no retained entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: groupMatchedItems and its callers show the literal is assigned once when the dynamic group is created.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Item counts vary by installed customizations, but the changed constant adds no per-item operation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no added synchronous loop, layout read, allocation scaling factor, or boundary call.

Scenarios.Scenario: Display Agent Host isolation choices and register the local terminal entry
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The isolation picker takes the static enum branch and returns two in-memory items; the changed text is one description. Terminal enablement registers one in-memory entry whose changed text is its name; getConnection remains lazy until use.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed two-item isolation choice and one local terminal entry; neither scales with sessions or hosts due to the label change.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Static picker item creation and terminal registry mutation are synchronous. No subprocess or IPC is started by either changed line.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Dynamic completion caching is bypassed by the static isolation branch. Terminal registration remains guarded by the existing MutableDisposable, so repeated enable/start events do not add duplicate entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the static early-return branch and guarded registration were inspected directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for the changed mechanism; both changed values are fixed strings.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the rename neither invokes provider completions nor changes terminal connection creation frequency.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The provider synchronously reads configuration/service state, pushes localized strings into an array, joins them, and constructs AccessibleContentProvider. Changed help paragraphs only replace words within existing entries.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed number of help paragraphs controlled by feature flags; work does not scale with sessions, providers, or history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous content construction; no asynchronous scheduling or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache key or retained collection is changed. Content size grows by a small fixed number of characters per help invocation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete provider construction path shows only local service/config reads and fixed string accumulation for the changed entries.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Localization can vary string lengths, but the fixed-size difference cannot establish meaningful CPU, memory, or layout regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: only constant-size text changes occur, with no new boundary or repeated scaling work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 16 changed files and every diff page. Production changes are localized label/documentation replacements; traced picker, filter, customization, Agent Host, terminal, and accessibility paths retain their prior cardinality, cache lifecycle, concurrency, and expensive-boundary behavior. No findings or regression-fix learning records were warranted.
